nba.team_glass_strategy.label: Offensive-glass crash rate versus transition-defense tradeoff of each team and coach
nba.team_glass_strategy.measurement: Compute per team-season OREB% and opponent transition points per possession after offensive rebounds (from play-by-play possession types) with 70-game half-life and coach-tenure reset; build matchup term = own crash rate x opponent weakness against crashing (opponent's DREB% minus expected from size) and report separately for OREB and DREB attributable to the player's position.
nba.team_glass_strategy.mechanism: Coaches choose how many players crash the offensive boards; heavy crashing raises OREB for bigs and lowers the opponent's DREB share while increasing transition possessions for opponents.
nba.team_glass_strategy.rationale: Crash policy is a team trait that is persistent across seasons within a coach, and it changes both rebound counts and pace; it is not recoverable from rebound pool or pace alone.

nba.team_points_margin_curve.label: Expected team points as a function of the game's expected margin (winner-loser asymmetry and garbage-time shape)
nba.team_points_margin_curve.measurement: From 5 seasons of games compute realised team points minus rating-based expected points as a function of pregame expected margin built from ratings (not the spread) in bins of 2 points; fit a monotone-spline of own points on expected margin with total environment as a covariate; use leave-one-season-out cross-validation; output expected team points given expected margin and total. Vintage rule: every team rating used (nba.off_rtg, nba.def_rtg, nba.lineup_adj_rating) must be the snapshot computed from games completed before that historical game's tipoff, stored daily over the 5 seasons, with the confirmed-inactive adjustment as of the pregame report; end-of-season or later-revised ratings are not allowed, as they leak the game's own result.
nba.team_points_margin_curve.mechanism: A team's points are not linear in the expected margin: favorites' points flatten (garbage time) and underdogs gain late points through fouling and deep-bench scoring, so the mapping from win probability to team points is a curve.
nba.team_points_margin_curve.rationale: Deriving team totals as (total ± spread)/2 assumes linearity; the empirical curve can differ by 1-2 points at large spreads, and this matters for strikes in a market keyed to the team's own points.
raw_data: team-game points, pregame expected margin from ratings

nba.team_points_variance_by_style.label: Style-dependent variance of a team's points (three-point reliance, transition share, pace)
nba.team_points_variance_by_style.measurement: Compute each team's residual sd of points (actual minus rating-based expectation, no market lines) over a season with regression on three-point attempt rate, pace and opponent style; shrink to league sd (about 12.5) with prior weight 25 games; combine own sd and opponent style effects; model the points distribution as skew-normal with skew from blowout probability. As-of: games before tip. Also output tail quantiles of own team points (80th, 90th, 95th and 99th percentile) and P(points >= strike) at strikes far above the mean, separately for a regulation-only and an overtime-included version, because far-away strikes (such as 135.5) are priced by the tail (three-point shooting variance, overtime) and not by the mean.
nba.team_points_variance_by_style.mechanism: Teams that take many threes and play fast have higher game-to-game variance in points than slow half-court teams; the over/under probability at a given strike depends on the sd, not only the mean.
nba.team_points_variance_by_style.rationale: A team total strike near the mean has probability near 50% regardless of variance, but strikes at 5-10 points away depend on the sd; the sd is team- and matchup-specific and is typically 11-14 points.

nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.label: Dependence between teams' records via head-to-head games and conference schedule overlap
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.measurement: From the remaining schedule compute pairwise numbers of head-to-head games and common-opponent overlap; in the simulation draw correlated team-strength shocks and enforce zero-sum head-to-head results; estimate the covariance of final win totals across the top-8 contenders by simulation; output distribution of the maximum and the probability of ties (tie handling per rule). As-of: nightly.
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.mechanism: Records of contending teams are not independent: when two top teams play each other, one gains what the other loses, and shared opponents create correlation in schedule luck.
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.rationale: Best-record and most-wins markets are about the maximum over teams, so the covariance of wins across teams matters; ignoring head-to-head linkage and common opponents misstates the extreme's distribution.

nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.label: Team-stat pair difference model (shared-pace correlation)
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.measurement: For team stat X (e.g. 3PM): mean_X = attempts_X × rate_X using opponent-adjusted rates (20-game half-life, k=150 attempts); sd_diff from joint empirical covariance over 3 seasons: var = var_A + var_B - 2 rho sd_A sd_B with rho from pace; compute P(A>B), P(tie) with discrete negative binomial convolution; blowout correction increasing trailing-team attempts.
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.mechanism: The head-to-head team stat is the difference of two counts with positive correlation through game pace and negative through script effects.
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.rationale: Treating the two teams' counts as independent overstates the sd of the difference and misprices the zero-tie mass.

free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com team and opponent shooting dashboards
nba.team_three_attempt_matchup.label: Team three-point attempt rate versus opponent 3PA allowed
nba.team_three_attempt_matchup.measurement: Team 3PA per 100 possessions (EWMA, 15-game half-life, shrunk to team prior season with weight 20 games) multiplied by opponent 3PA-allowed index (opponent 3PA allowed per 100 / league mean, 20-game half-life, shrunk with weight 25 games); expected 3PA = index-adjusted rate x projected game possessions / 100, adjusted for missing high-volume shooters via player 3PA shares; make rate from nba.three_pt_luck expectation; as-of: games completed before the market's snapshot.
nba.team_three_attempt_matchup.mechanism: Team made threes = possessions x team 3PA per possession x make rate; the 3PA share is a stable team-scheme trait modulated by how many threes the opponent's defence concedes.
nba.team_three_attempt_matchup.rationale: KXNBAH2HTEAM3PT is settled on made threes, and attempt volume (25-45 3PA per team-game across the league) separates teams far more than 3P%; a high-volume team facing a defence that runs opponents off the line loses much of its edge, which ratings and pace inputs do not capture.

nba.team_win_streak_hazard.label: Hazard of a team reaching a 20-game winning streak (run-length chain with heterogeneous game win probabilities)
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.measurement: For each team and each window of 20 consecutive scheduled games compute the product of game win probabilities from ratings and rest (with a star-health scenario mixture); P(streak >= 20 for team i) = 1 - prod over windows via a Markov chain with state = current run length; combine across teams assuming approximate independence except head-to-head links; include Cup games (they count) and exclude the Cup final and playoffs. As-of: nightly; update current runs.
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.mechanism: A 20-game win streak requires 20 consecutive wins; with game win probabilities of 75-85% for the best team, the chance depends on the full sequence of probabilities, their correlation through star health and schedule, and the number of teams that could qualify.
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.rationale: Averaging a team's win probability underestimates the chance because a streak concentrates in stretches of weak opponents and healthy rosters; the league-wide market is a union over 30 teams and 63 windows each (82 games minus 19).
raw_data: schedule with opponents and dates, ratings, current run length per team

nba.teammate_absence_shift.label: With/without teammate splits: usage, minutes and stat redistribution
nba.teammate_absence_shift.measurement: Per player: stat per minute and minutes with teammate X on/off the roster, over games where X missed; hierarchical shrinkage to a role-based redistribution model (usage, ball handling, rebound share absorbed); evaluate for combinations of absences.
nba.teammate_absence_shift.mechanism: When key teammates are out, shot attempts, ball-handling, and rebound opportunities redistribute to the remaining players in a structured way (not evenly).
nba.teammate_absence_shift.rationale: This is the largest edge source for props: a lead guard out raises the backup guard's usage and assists, but a primary scorer out lowers assists for his passing partner (fewer converted passes). Direction depends on whether the absent player consumes the stat (usage, rebounds) or produces teammates' stat conversion (shooters). Subtle: with/without samples are small and confounded by opponent and by injuries to multiple players; use hierarchical shrinkage and role-based priors.

nba.teammate_conv.label: Teammate shot conversion / shooting quality
nba.teammate_conv.measurement: AST/potential assist history; expected conversion = sum over teammates of pass share x teammate expected eFG given shot type; use shrinkage; condition on which teammates are active tonight.
nba.teammate_conv.mechanism: Assists depend on whether the shots a player creates are made; the shooting skill and shot quality of teammates on the floor raises or lowers conversion.
nba.teammate_conv.rationale: Teammate expected eFG on the passes created (shooters like catch-and-shoot specialists vs low-percentage players) changes assists per potential assist from ~0.4 to ~0.6. Subtle: conversion has luck (hot/cold shooters) that should be regressed, but real roster quality changes (star shooter returning or leaving) is real signal.
raw_data: assisted field goals by passer-shooter pair

nba.three_att_script_elasticity.label: Elasticity of a shooter's three-point attempt rate to score margin and quarter
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.measurement: From play-by-play estimate per player 3PA per minute in margin bins (<-12, -12..-5, -5..+5, +5..+12, >+12) by quarter, with empirical-Bayes shrinkage to role-archetype bins (prior weight 120 minutes per bin); combine with the projected distribution of margin paths from team ratings (not the spread). Output expected 3PA integrating over the margin-path distribution and minutes mixture.
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.mechanism: Trailing teams take more threes late and leading teams run clock and bench shooters, so 3PA per minute is a function of the margin path, not a constant.
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.rationale: Blowout dynamics cut starters but raise bench shooters' attempts; a close fourth quarter raises volume for closers; the sign differs between roles, so a single 'blowout' penalty misprices spot-up wings and bench shooters.
raw_data: PBP shot events with score margin, player minutes by bin

nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.label: Hierarchical make probability by shot type (catch-and-shoot vs pull-up) and defender openness
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.measurement: Base model (public per-shot data): beta-binomial hierarchy on made/attempted by shot zone (corner, above the break) x pull-up flag from shotchartdetail ACTION_TYPE and SHOT_ZONE fields over 3 seasons, league-cell mean as prior with prior weight 250 attempts per cell, partial pooling by player, recent-season weight 0.5 per year. Optional refinement if the tracking dashboards are confirmed (p3-defender-distance): aggregate catch-and-shoot versus pull-up and closest-defender bins (wide open 6+ ft, open 4-6, tight under 4) as separate multiplicative adjustments, not a crossed cell, because the dashboards are not per-shot. Combine with tonight's predicted context mix from shot-creation role and opponent openness allowed. Output a single p3 with credible interval. As-of: shots finished before tip.
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.mechanism: Make probability depends on shot context more than on a single season 3P%, so talent should be estimated per context and recombined with tonight's expected context mix.
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.rationale: Overall 3P% averages over open catch-and-shoot threes (about 38%) and tightly contested pull-ups (about 31%); a shooter's attempt mix changes with teammates and opposing closeouts, so the make probability changes even with fixed talent.
raw_data: shot-level 3PA with zone, action type and result (shotchartdetail)

nba.three_point_variance_load.label: Three-point attempt volume as a variance load
nba.three_point_variance_load.measurement: Var_total = Σ_team [9*3PA*p3(1-p3) + 4*2PA*p2(1-p2) + FTA*pft(1-pft)] + var(possessions)*ppp^2*... using opponent-adjusted attempts and rates (20-game half-life); calibrate a scale factor lambda so that predicted variance matches realised total residual variance in 2 prior seasons; report sd per game and skew.
nba.three_point_variance_load.mechanism: The sd of the total depends on how many threes both teams attempt and on the dispersion of free-throw and two-point results.
nba.three_point_variance_load.rationale: The draft says total sd is about 17-19 as a constant; it varies with shot mix, and wide-open three-heavy teams produce a wider total distribution that matters at ladder tails.

nba.three_pt_luck.label: Team three-point shooting luck vs shot quality (own and opponent)
nba.three_pt_luck.measurement: Expected 3P% = sum over attempts of shooter prior (career/regressed) adjusted for openness; luck = actual - expected over trailing N games; estimate shrinkage factor from out-of-sample reversion; same for opponent 3P% allowed with league-mean prior weighted heavily.
nba.three_pt_luck.mechanism: Realized team 3P% regresses toward a shot-quality-based expectation; opponent 3P% allowed is mostly outside the defense's control on open looks.
nba.three_pt_luck.rationale: Hot or cold shooting streaks inflate or deflate recent offensive/defensive ratings and totals; ignoring regression overstates how hot teams will score and how stingy lucky defenses are. Subtle: shooters' true skill still differs, so expectation must use shooter-specific priors and shot openness, not a league mean.
raw_data: team and opponent 3P% vs shot quality

nba.three_volume.label: 3PA rate, catch-and-shoot share, 3P% shrinkage and opponent 3PA allowed
nba.three_volume.measurement: 3PA per 36 (EWMA), catch-and-shoot vs pull-up share, shot openness; 3P% shrunk with beta prior (career/team) with prior weight about 200-300 attempts; opponent 3PA allowed per 100 relative to league; negative-binomial attempts model.
nba.three_volume.mechanism: Threes made equal attempts times make probability; attempts are driven by role, minutes and opponent scheme, and make% must be shrunk heavily.
nba.three_volume.rationale: A player's 3PA per minute is much more stable than 3P%; make% over a season reverts toward career and shot-quality-based expectation. Opponent 3PA allowed and pace/spacing change attempt volume. Subtle: attempts are overdispersed (game-to-game volume varies), so a binomial with fixed attempts understates variance.

nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.label: Three-Point Contest round-score distribution and winner simulation
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.measurement: For each entrant simulate ball by ball: P(make) per location from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile (regular, money-ball and deep-zone balls), the shooter's chosen all-money-ball rack location, balls actually released within 70 s from the tempo distribution (unreleased balls score 0), rack-level correlation rho with a beta-binomial prior from nba.within_game_make_dispersion, point weights from nba.contest_format_rules_ledger; run 20000 simulations of round 1, top-three advancement, final round (score resets) and a shoot-off on ties; output P(win), P(advance). As-of = last field change or rack-placement announcement.
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.mechanism: Each shooter's round score is a sum over racks of correlated Bernoulli makes with different point weights; the winner is the maximum over finalists after advancement, with ties broken by a shoot-off.
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.rationale: The winner is a max-of-noisy-scores over a field of about eight, so the favourite's chance is capped well below his skill edge; the round-score SD is several points, comparable to the skill gap between the best and median shooter (per-ball make probability is a parameter to be estimated, not a fact). Only the final-round score decides (rules), so round-1 advancement variance and final-round tie mass both matter.

free_sources: NBA Stats shot dashboard and shot-location splits
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.label: Three-point contest location, deep-ball and release-tempo profile per shooter
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.measurement: Per shooter: catch-and-shoot 3P% by zone (left corner, right corner, left wing, right wing, top), last 3 seasons, each shrunk to his own pooled rate with k=150 attempts (placeholder); 27+ ft 3P% shrunk to league deep rate with k=100; tempo = balls released per round and seconds left in past contests (median and SD), else imputed from catch-and-shoot release time; rack-placement = announced choice, else the zone maximizing expected points; units = P(make) by ball type and balls released; as-of = rack announcement.
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.mechanism: Contest score depends on accuracy at each rack location, on deep-range accuracy for the bonus balls between racks, on where the shooter places the all-money-ball rack, and on how many balls he releases before 70 seconds expire.
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.rationale: Pooled open 3P% hides location splits: a corner specialist gains by placing the all-money rack in his best corner, and the deep bonus balls reward a 27+ ft make rate that many spot-up shooters lack. The 70-second limit (rules) means slow releasers leave balls unshot, a zero that pooled accuracy never sees.
raw_data: shot-level 3PA with x,y location and distance

nba.tiebreak_ledger.label: Head-to-head, division and conference record ledger for tiebreaker evaluation
nba.tiebreak_ledger.measurement: For each team pair compute season-to-date head-to-head wins/losses and remaining games, division record, conference record and record vs playoff teams, updated nightly from game results; in the simulation, apply the official tiebreak procedure (stored as code from league rules) to simulated ties and output P(win tie) by pair. As-of: nightly after final scores.
nba.tiebreak_ledger.mechanism: Seeds and division winners are decided by the league's tiebreak hierarchy (head-to-head, division winner, conference record and so on), so exact ties are resolved by information that accumulates over the season.
nba.tiebreak_ledger.rationale: Simulating only win totals misses the probability that a tie is broken in a team's favor; at seed boundaries (6th vs 7th, 10th vs 11th, play-in cutoff) a tie occurs in about 8-15% of final standings and the tiebreak ledger is partly known before the season ends.
raw_data: game results by pair, schedule, division/conference identifiers

nba.title_path.label: Playoff bracket path, matchup and home-court structure
nba.title_path.measurement: Simulate bracket with seed distribution and series-level win probability; incorporate matchup tweaks (style, pace, rim protection) and home-court structure (2-2-1-1-1).
nba.title_path.mechanism: Series winner and title probabilities depend on the bracket path (seed, opponent strength, home-court) and matchup-specific adjustments.
nba.title_path.rationale: Title odds are the product of series-win probabilities along a path that depends on which seed you are, who you face and the rest/injury states. A given team's path difficulty can differ substantially even for equal rating. Subtle: series outcomes are correlated through injuries to key players across rounds.

free_sources: NBA.com transaction log with processing dates
nba.top_pick_trade_hazard.label: Top-10 draft pick trade hazard (pick or draft rights, processed in window)
nba.top_pick_trade_hazard.measurement: From 15 drafts count, per draft, whether any top-10 pick or its rights was traded and the processing date (pre-draft, draft night pick-for-pick, post-moratorium); P(Yes) = P(any top-10 pick trade agreed by the window) x P(processed by window end | deal type), with deal type inferred from whether salaried players are included; condition on the number of top-10 picks held by win-now teams and the board's consensus tightness; as-of: market snapshot.
nba.top_pick_trade_hazard.mechanism: Top-10 picks are traded when a team's valuation of the pick differs from another's (consensus-board gaps, win-now teams with picks), and only trades officially processed in the window count.
nba.top_pick_trade_hazard.rationale: KXNBAPICKTRADE counts a trade of any top-10 pick or of a drafted player's rights before he signs, officially processed before the window end; many draft-night deals are agreed then processed after the moratorium, so the agreement base rate overstates Yes.
raw_data: draft-day trade list with agreement and processing dates

nba.undefeated_start_survival.label: Survival probability of undefeated starts by calendar day (last remaining unbeaten team)
nba.undefeated_start_survival.measurement: For each team compute S_i(d) = product over games on days <= d of P(win) (from ratings, rest and home/away); P(team i is the last undefeated) = sum over days of P(i's first loss on day d and all others have lost by day d), with ties on the same day sharing 1/N; compute by simulation with dependence from shared opponents. As-of: nightly; early in the season (about 8-10 games played) the field is nearly resolved.
nba.undefeated_start_survival.mechanism: The last undefeated team is the one whose first loss comes latest, measured by the date of the first loss, so the market depends on survival functions of each team and ties by date.
nba.undefeated_start_survival.rationale: The product of win probabilities gives each team's survival, but the contract resolves by the day of the first loss and splits ties when several teams lose on the same day, so the probability of a team being last depends on ties and calendar clustering.
raw_data: schedule with dates, ratings, current records

nba.unsigned_player_signing_hazard.label: Unsigned-player NBA signing and activation hazard
nba.unsigned_player_signing_hazard.measurement: Reference class of unsigned veterans aged 26+ with prior NBA rotation roles (2010-2026) at the same calendar date: monthly signing hazard by age, last-season minutes and games, injury status, minimum-contract interest reports; P(play | signed) from the share of such signings that logged regular-season minutes and days to first appearance; combine over remaining regular-season dates; as-of: market snapshot.
nba.unsigned_player_signing_hazard.mechanism: An unsigned veteran appears in a regular-season game only after a team signs him and plays him; signings cluster at camp, injury waves and the buyout window.
nba.unsigned_player_signing_hazard.rationale: KXNBACOMPETE needs at least one second of regular-season play by an unsigned player, so the probability is P(sign before the season's last games) x P(play | signed); health and perceived value drive the signing, and a late signing leaves few games, which a generic availability input does not model.

nba.usage_allocation_model.label: Lineup-conditional shot-attempt allocation model for tonight's expected on-court unit
nba.usage_allocation_model.measurement: Fit a Dirichlet-multinomial (or softmax) model of FGA+0.44*FTA+TOV shares among the five on-court players using stint data, with player creation archetype, on-ball minutes share and prior-season usage as features; ridge-regularised, 2-season window with 200-game half-life; predict tonight's shares for the projected unit set (weighted by expected minutes per unit) and report mean and standard error. As-of: injury report at last vintage.
nba.usage_allocation_model.mechanism: Team attempts are a roughly fixed pie divided among the five on court according to creation roles, so a scorer's share is a function of the whole unit, not just whether one named teammate is out.
nba.usage_allocation_model.rationale: With/without splits rest on tiny samples and ignore that replacing a creator by a catch-and-shoot wing shifts shots differently than replacing him by another creator; an allocation model with role types generalises across rosters.
raw_data: lineup stints possessions, FGA, FTA, TOV by player

nba.voter_signal_proxy.label: Observable voter-signal proxy: public media ladders, prior-win count and repeat-winner penalty
nba.voter_signal_proxy.measurement: For each candidate and award: mean rank over the last 4 published media ladders (NBA.com ladder, ESPN straw poll; unranked = 6th) with weights 0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 newest first; repeat_penalty = number of consecutive prior wins; prior_share = first-place vote share in the last two seasons (0 if not a finalist); fit a conditional-logit ballot model on 2000-2026 winners with these three features plus production rank and seed, shrinking coefficients with a ridge penalty chosen by leave-one-season-out.
nba.voter_signal_proxy.mechanism: Replaces the unmeasurable narrative and voter-fatigue notion with observables: average rank in published media award ladders and straw polls, the number of consecutive prior wins, and the candidate's first-place share in the previous two seasons.
nba.voter_signal_proxy.rationale: nba.voting_narrative is audited WEAK because it is not measurable as defined, yet narrative and fatigue are the only drivers of the vote beyond production and team success; a proxy built from public ladders and past ballots gives them a measurable form without using any market price.

nba.within_game_make_dispersion.label: Within-game make-rate dispersion (beta-binomial rho)
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.measurement: Estimate rho by maximum likelihood of a beta-binomial model on 5 seasons of player-game (attempts, makes) for players with at least 200 attempts; pool by shot type (three, two, free throw) and by attempt count; shrink the player-specific rho to the pooled value with k=100 games; produce the pmf of makes given attempts n and rate p.
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.mechanism: Makes in a game are positively correlated beyond independent shots, so the count is overdispersed relative to a binomial.
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.rationale: Independence understates the tail of makes, which a convex payout over-weights; the dispersion parameter is a key tail parameter.
raw_data: player-game attempts and makes by type

nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.label: Within-team scoring allocation dependence
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.measurement: For each team and pair of top-6 players, compute the correlation of player points conditional on team points (partial correlation) using 3 seasons of games, shrunk to the role-pair prior with k=40 games; combine with team total correlation to get unconditional pairwise correlations; separate regimes with/without a major teammate absence.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.mechanism: Teammates split a fixed team total, giving negative dependence between teammates' counts conditional on team points.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.rationale: Treating two teammates' overs as positively dependent through the team total omits the allocation effect that offsets it at fixed pace; the net sign depends on how much variation in the team total versus in the split drives each leg.
